choices.text: The student is right - logistic growth is just exponential growth with a bigger rate
As the population nears the carrying capacity K the growth rate falls to zero, so the curve bends over and levels at P = K, the stable equilibrium every starting population is funnelled to.
Only the first doubling counts towards the population
The population grows by more each step near K, not less

questions.feedback: If you agreed with the student, that is the trap: The population keeps growing faster and faster like a pure exponential, so it never slows down or levels off. Reteach point: As the population nears the carrying capacity K the growth rate falls to zero, so the curve bends over and levels at P = K, the stable equilibrium every starting population is funnelled to.
questions.misconception: The population keeps growing faster and faster like a pure exponential, so it never slows down or levels off.
questions.prompt: A student says the population keeps growing faster and faster like a pure exponential, so it never levels off. What is the best correction?

questions.answer: At P = K the factor (1 - P/K) in dP/dt = rP(1 - P/K) is zero, so dP/dt is zero and the population stops changing.
questions.feedback: A strong answer names the factor: (1 - P/K) hits zero exactly at the carrying capacity.
questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain why the growth rate is zero at P = K.

choices.text: It keeps rising, because it started high
It falls back down and settles at P = K
It stays flat wherever it started

questions.feedback: Scene 2 shows the high start: above K the growth rate is negative, so the curve falls back and settles at P = K.
questions.prompt: A population starts above the carrying capacity K. What does its curve do?

questions.answer: The equilibrium drops to a lower level and the population re-settles there, because steady harvesting removes population every season so the old K no longer balances.
questions.feedback: Credit the lower re-settle point with harvesting reasoning: removals drag the balancing level below the old K.
questions.prompt: Harvesting starts on a settled population. State what happens to the equilibrium, and say how you know.
